authority: Governor, state legislature, regulators and local permitting bodies have different powers
observed_remedy: Public support for at least a one-year ban; no enacted statewide moratorium established by this evidence packet
election_link: November 3 gubernatorial and legislative contests; governor's new term begins January 2027. August 11 nomination resolution and turnout-screen differences confound attribution of the odds change.
cross_party_status: Opposition to the cost-benefit balance spans Republican, independent and Democratic respondents; party-specific support for the same ban is not established here.
cash_flow_channel: Prospective permitting, infrastructure cost allocation and development timing; do not assume all existing facilities are affected equally.
interpretation: Broad concern is established; data centers are a much smaller stated current priority than inflation.

authority: Public Utilities Commission of Ohio; AEP Ohio tariff process
observed_remedy: Separate data-center tariff addressing stranded infrastructure and cost shifting; order also called for lifting AEP Ohio's connection moratorium
election_link: Existing regulatory action predates this campaign; changing the governor does not itself rewrite every approved utility tariff.
cross_party_status: This regulatory order does not measure partisan voter agreement.
cash_flow_channel: Customer commitments and minimum charges can protect utility recovery while raising the hurdle for new data-center customers.
interpretation: Cost protection can enable connection growth; it is not equivalent to banning development.

authority: Governor and permitting agencies; utility tariffs still require the appropriate PUC process
observed_remedy: GRID participation and local-approval sequencing for new applications above 25 MW; data centers removed from Fast Track; advocacy for protective tariffs
election_link: Executive implementation is already underway before the November gubernatorial vote; distinguish incumbent actions from future legislative capacity.
cross_party_status: An executive order is institutional action, not a measure of bipartisan voter or legislative support.
cash_flow_channel: Timing, project financing and infrastructure obligations may change without a universal ban or cancellation of all orders.
interpretation: The immediate investable risk is conditional development and who pays, not a categorical statewide prohibition.

authority: Governor, legislature, Department of Energy Resources and utility regulator
observed_remedy: Moratorium bill veto sustained; advisory council created; recommendations due January 29, 2027
election_link: The recommendations fall after the election; the sustained veto shows that public pressure and enacted restrictions can diverge.
cross_party_status: Governor supported a temporary moratorium with a project exemption; not a simple pro-development versus anti-development division.
cash_flow_channel: Project-specific employment and local tax-base benefits can alter exemptions and legislative compromises.
interpretation: Policy design and exemptions matter; the advisory council cannot be counted as a binding moratorium.

observed_remedy: Enacted automated-decision rules covering consequential decisions; major developer duties and attorney-general rules from January 2027
election_link: Implementation follows the election but arises from an existing law; a new governor does not make the law disappear automatically.
cross_party_status: Recorded majorities are 34-1 Senate and 57-6 House; no party affiliation is inferred from vote totals.
cash_flow_channel: Documentation, notices, human review and record retention affect covered applications; do not apply indiscriminately to every AI revenue stream.
interpretation: Concrete state compliance risk exists even without a new federal AI act.
